claims.text: Thermally activated short-range order is the single mechanistic driver unifying the stress–strain and thermoelastic behavior of HfNbTaTiZr.
Enhanced short-range order produces local lattice distortions.
SRO-associated lattice distortions modify dislocation drag and internal stress fields.
SRO-mediated changes in dislocation behavior increase creep resistance.
SRO alters the elastic moduli of HfNbTaTiZr.
SRO alters the thermal-expansion behavior of HfNbTaTiZr.
As-cast HfNbTaTiZr has a nearly random solid-solution structure.
Heat treatments at 600–800 °C promote SRO development in HfNbTaTiZr.
Rapid quenching suppresses SRO and yields a nearly random-solid-solution baseline.
SRO changes the distribution and magnitude of local lattice strains.
Changes in local lattice strain alter dislocation–solute interactions and dislocation drag.
SRO affects creep and thermoelastic properties by changing internal stress fields and deformation energy barriers.
SRO-enhanced samples will have greater creep resistance at 1250 °C than rapidly quenched samples.
SRO-enhanced samples will show more pronounced hardening after aging at 600–800 °C than rapidly quenched samples.
SRO-enhanced and rapidly quenched samples will have measurably different elastic moduli and thermal-expansion coefficients.
The degree of SRO will correlate consistently with the measured mechanical and thermoelastic properties.
The strongest SRO-driven property changes are expected during or after heat treatment at 600–800 °C.

contradictions.description: The intervention says intermediate-temperature heat treatments are coupled with a rapid quench 'to serve as a SRO-suppressed baseline,' whereas the baseline and experimental design describe the quenched material as a separate set. Quenching after an SRO-promoting treatment is not clearly distinguished from quenching a sample before such ordering develops.
